questions.scenario: You order from Swiggy/Zomato and the delivery is delayed by 40 minutes. What goes through your mind?

options.text: You chat with the delivery bhaiya when he arrives to ask if the app showed him the wrong map or if traffic was bad.
You wonder how the app calculates the 'Estimated Time of Arrival' algorithm and how often it is actually accurate.
You get annoyed at the live-tracking screen and imagine a cleaner, more accurate map animation to show the bike's exact lane.
You think offering a 'Guaranteed 30-min or free' feature would get them way more orders, even if they have to pay some refunds.

questions.scenario: A new Math tuition class opens in your locality and suddenly every student wants to join it. Why do you think it's successful?

options.text: You ask 3 friends who joined it to find out if they actually like the teaching style or just go because their friends go.
You mentally calculate the teacher's revenue: 50 students × Rs. 2000 fees per month = Rs. 1 Lakh from one batch!
You notice the tuition center has an AC, modern whiteboards, and cool printed notes instead of boring old blackboards.
You think about how the teacher could scale up by recording his lectures and selling them on a pen-drive across the city.

questions.scenario: Your family WhatsApp group is blasting with 'Good Morning' forwards. How would you fix this?

options.text: You try to understand the psychology behind why uncles and aunties feel the need to send these daily to show affection.
You wish WhatsApp had a dashboard showing exactly how many gigabytes of phone storage these forwards are wasting across India.
You imagine a smart, hidden 'Zen Mode' toggle that automatically blurs out messages containing flowers and sunrises.
You realize WhatsApp could make millions if they offered an 'Auto-clean' premium subscription for family groups.

questions.scenario: You are helping your mom buy a new smartphone on Flipkart. What is your strategy?

options.text: Observe how she holds her current phone and ask her what she finds most frustrating about typing messages.
Filter by specifications: Compare the RAM, battery mAh, and processor benchmark scores between 4 different models.
Focus on the design: Ensure the phone isn't too heavy, has a premium matte finish, and comes in her favorite pastel color.
Check the exchange offer value, bank card discounts, and calculate if buying during the Big Billion Days sale makes the most sense.

questions.scenario: You are playing a multiplayer game like BGMI or Free Fire with friends, but the new update is terrible.

options.text: Read the Reddit and YouTube comment sections to see if other players are complaining about the exact same issues.
Realize that the heavy new map graphics are probably dropping the frame rate (FPS) on average mid-range Indian phones.
Hate the new complicated lobby menu and wish the developers would go back to the old, simple button layout.
Predict that if the company doesn't release a patch in 3 days, they will lose millions of daily active users to their competitor.

questions.scenario: You are trying to book a Tatkal train ticket on IRCTC and the website is lagging right at 10:00 AM.

options.text: Feel the frustration of senior citizens who must struggle even more, and ask your dad how he usually manages to get a ticket.
Wonder about the server load capacity and exactly how many lakh concurrent users hit the 'Book Now' button at the same second.
Want to redesign the entire messy homepage to make the 'From', 'To', and 'Date' search bars the only big, clean things on the screen.
Think the government should introduce a premium 'Server Priority' fee for people willing to pay Rs. 100 extra to skip the queue.

questions.scenario: You are watching a terrible, boring movie at PVR on a Sunday. What are you doing?

options.text: Watching the audience's faces in the theater to see exactly which scenes make them yawn or pull out their phones.
Mentally calculating the box office opening numbers and figuring out how much they wasted on marketing vs. production.
Criticizing the terrible CGI VFX, the weird camera angles, and the completely mismatching background score.
Wondering why they didn't cut the movie by 30 minutes to fit in more showtimes per day and sell more popcorn.

questions.scenario: A fancy new Momos and Boba Tea cafe opens near your society. What is your observation?

options.text: You chat with the owner and the first few customers to see if the expensive Boba taste actually suits the local Indian palate.
You notice that maximum footfall happens strictly between 5 PM and 7 PM right after the local tuition classes end.
You love the neon lights, the comfortable seating arrangement, and how highly Instagrammable the transparent cups are.
You figure out that keeping the momos cheap but pricing the drinks super high is a brilliant profit margin strategy.

questions.scenario: You are organizing the core committee for the 10th standard school farewell party. What is your role?

options.text: Taking a quick poll among sections A, B, and C to find out what kind of DJ music and food menu everyone actually wants.
Looking at last year's budget to calculate the exact per-head cost and identify where maximum money was wasted.
Focusing completely on the stage decoration theme, the photo-booth props, and the aesthetic font of the e-invites.
Negotiating hard with the local caterer to get a 15% discount so you have extra funds to hire a much better DJ.

questions.scenario: For a school science project, your team has to invent a 'Smart Water Bottle'. What do you suggest?

options.text: Interviewing your classmates first to find out the exact psychological reason why they forget to drink water during school hours.
Adding a sensor that tracks exactly how many ml of water the user drinks daily and graphs it over a week on a companion app.
Designing a sleek bottle with a cool LED ring that glows softly to remind you to drink, without making the bottle look bulky.
Figuring out the wholesale manufacturing cost in markets like Sadar Bazaar so you can price it to make a solid 50% profit margin.

User_Researcher.title: The Empathy Engine (User Researcher)
User_Researcher.primary_match_text: You love understanding people. You are observant, a great listener, and always want to know *why* someone behaves the way they do. You build things for real human beings, not just for machines.
User_Researcher.day_in_the_life: Talking to real users, conducting surveys, observing how people struggle with apps, and telling the tech team what the public actually wants and needs.
User_Researcher.alternative_match_text: Your high emotional intelligence would also make you a fantastic Psychologist, Journalist, or Sociologist.
User_Researcher.educational_roadmap: 11th/12th: Any stream (Humanities/Arts is great). Degree: B.A. in Psychology, Sociology, or B.Des. Next Steps: Look for specialized courses in Human-Computer Interaction (HCI) or Behavioral Science.

Data_PM.title: The Logic Master (Data-Driven PM)
Data_PM.primary_match_text: You trust numbers over opinions. You are analytical, love finding patterns, and want to make decisions backed by solid proof and statistics. You don't guess; you measure.
Data_PM.day_in_the_life: Staring at dashboards, running A/B tests to see if a red or green button gets more clicks, and analyzing exactly where users uninstall the app.
Data_PM.alternative_match_text: Your love for numbers and logic makes you a perfect fit for Data Science, Financial Analysis, or Software Engineering.
Data_PM.educational_roadmap: 11th/12th: Commerce with Math or Science (PCM). Degree: B.Tech, B.Sc in Statistics, or BBA. Next Steps: Learn SQL, Python, and master Product Analytics tools like Mixpanel.

UX_Design_PM.title: The Experience Architect (UX/Design PM)
UX_Design_PM.primary_match_text: You care deeply about how things look and feel. You hate messy, confusing interfaces and want technology to be beautiful, simple, and completely intuitive to use.
UX_Design_PM.day_in_the_life: Creating wireframes, choosing color palettes, deciding the exact flow from the home screen to the checkout page, and working closely with graphic designers.
UX_Design_PM.alternative_match_text: If not Product Management, your visual creativity would make you a brilliant UI/UX Designer, Front-End Developer, or Creative Director.
UX_Design_PM.educational_roadmap: 11th/12th: Any stream. Entrance: Crack UCEED or NID exams. Degree: B.Des (Bachelor of Design) or a B.Tech/BCA while building a strong personal design portfolio.

Business_Strategy_PM.title: The Product CEO (Business / Strategy PM)
Business_Strategy_PM.primary_match_text: You are the ultimate planner and leader. You understand technology, but you focus on the big picture: how to make money, beat competitors, and lead a team to victory.
Business_Strategy_PM.day_in_the_life: Managing deadlines, deciding which feature the engineering team should build first, pitching to investors, and making sure the app makes maximum profit.
Business_Strategy_PM.alternative_match_text: Your leadership and business mindset would make you an excellent Entrepreneur, Management Consultant, or Marketing Head.
Business_Strategy_PM.educational_roadmap: 11th/12th: Commerce or Science. Degree: BBA, B.Com, or B.Tech. Next Steps: Work for a couple of years, crack the CAT/GMAT, and get an MBA from a top-tier institute like an IIM or ISB.
